proof_nl: Let x be an arbitrary real number, and set m = floor(x). By the defining property of the floor function, m is an integer such that m <= x < m + 1. Subtracting m from the inequality x < m + 1 gives x - m < 1. Since m = floor(x), this is exactly x - floor(x) < 1. Because x was arbitrary, the inequality holds for every real number x.
solver_summary: Using the defining property of the floor function, if m = floor(x) then m <= x < m+1, hence x - floor(x) = x - m < 1 for all real x.
vetter_reason: The proof correctly derives x - floor(x) < 1 from the defining property of floor and concludes universally by arbitrary x. It matches the lemma statement exactly and introduces no unsupported dependencies or semantic drift.
